paragraphs.text: Called Huram. {2Ch 2:3} Josephus calleth him Irom, and Eupolemus in Eusebius Suron. He was king of Tyre and Sidon also.
paragraphs.anchor: And Hiram.

paragraphs.text: A fast friend is a rare bird. Most friends now-a-days are like Joab’s dagger, as soon in and as soon out. The love of foster-brothers in Ireland far surpasseth - saith one, {a} but I believe him not - all the loves of all men. They only love truly that love one another out of a pure heart fervently. {1Pe 1:22} This love lasteth.
paragraphs.anchor: For Hiram was ever a lover of David.

paragraphs.text: {a} Camden’s Elisab., 483.
By the same messengers, say some. Rather by ambassadors of his own.
paragraphs.anchor: And Solomon sent to Hiram.

paragraphs.text: He saith not for his shedding of blood, which elsewhere is made the reason why David might not build a house, {1Ch 28:3} but only for his continual wars, by reason whereof he had not time to do it. The best things are to be spoken of parents: to speak evil to them, {a} or of them, was death by God’s law; {Mat 15:5} yea, by Solon’s laws, though a heathen.
paragraphs.anchor: For the wars that were about him.

paragraphs.text: {a} κακολογων.

The Vulgate hath it, Non est Satan. We use to say, Seldom lieth the devil dead in a ditch. He is the troublous one, {a} and delighteth to hinder anything that is good; but at this time God had chained him up, and Solomon had nothing to hinder him. "The Lord is with you, whilst ye are with him," saith one prophet. {2Ch 15:2} And, "The Lord will be with the good," saith another. {2Ch 19:11}
paragraphs.anchor: So that there is neither adversary.

paragraphs.text: {a} ο πονηρος.

Wherein he became a type of Christ, who buildeth his Church, that spiritual temple. See Isa 44:28 Mat 16:18. In the Old Testament the brass gates were opened to make way for the building of that temple; {Isa 45:2} but in the New, those gates of hell shall not gainstand, or prevail.
paragraphs.anchor: To build a house unto the name.

paragraphs.text: Solomon’s purpose was founded upon God’s gracious promise. This was a right rise, for want whereof many men’s purposes, like clouds without rain, vanish, and come to nothing.
paragraphs.anchor: As the Lord spake unto David.

paragraphs.text: Satan, though he could not hinder the building of the temple, {1Ki 5:4} yet he would needs imitate it, and, if possible, outdo it; for his temple of Diana, at Ephesus, was likewise built of cedar, as Vitruvius relateth, and was much longer and larger than this at Jerusalem, as others assure us.
paragraphs.anchor: That they hew me cedar trees out of Lebanon.

paragraphs.text: Only Jews meddled with the tabernacle; but the temple is not built without the aid of the Gentile Tyrians. They, together with us, make up the Church of God. See Eph 2:13-14.
paragraphs.anchor: And my servants shall be with thy servants.

paragraphs.text: Various men have their various gifts; and various countries their various abilities. These, as they have from God, so they must use them for him. {Isa 28:26; Isa 28:29 Rom 11:36}
paragraphs.anchor: That can skill to hew timber like unto the Sidonians.

paragraphs.text: His carefulness he improveth unto thankfulness, whence some conclude him a proselyted prince. And surely thankfulness to the true God is a good sign of true grace. The Greeks have but one word (χαρις) to signify both.
paragraphs.anchor: Blessed be the Lord this day.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Heard. A request is to be considered ere it be granted, lest men come in afterwards with the fool’s, Had I known. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: I have considered.

paragraphs.text: Whereof there was much use made about the temple. {1Ki 6:15} Algum trees also were sent from Lebanon, {2Ch 2:8} which were a wood that is unknown to us, but most precious.
paragraphs.anchor: And concerning timber of fir.

paragraphs.text: {a} ουκ ψμην.
To Joppa, {2Ch 2:16} which had a harbour. {Act 9:43}
paragraphs.anchor: Unto the place that thou shalt appoint me.

paragraphs.text: David had, before his death, prepared abundantly both workmen and cedar trees, &c., {1Ch 22:2-4; 1Ch 29:3} but yet nothing near enough for so great a work.
paragraphs.anchor: And thou shalt receive them.

paragraphs.text: Which in that country was a scarce commodity. They were supplied from other countries, and especially from Jewry; {Act 12:20 Eze 27:17} for their own was such as wherein they could neither sow nor reap, saith A. Lapide.
paragraphs.anchor: In giving food

paragraphs.text: Wherein he was as good as his word. {1Ki 5:8} Of many promisers it may be said, as Tertullian of the peacock, they are all in changeable colours, as often changed as moved,
paragraphs.anchor: According to all his desire.

paragraphs.text: “ Tantum constantes in levitate sua. ”
Here was fair and faithful dealing on both sides.
paragraphs.anchor: And Solomon gave Hiram.

paragraphs.text: “ In cuius subiere locum fraudesque, delique. ”
Besides twenty thousand measures of barley, and twenty thousand baths of oil, ordinary oil for the workmen, {2Ch 2:10} twenty thousand baths of wine also, not here mentioned.
paragraphs.anchor: Twenty thousand measures of wheat, &c.

paragraphs.text: Sapientiam architectonicam, tanquam Idaeam futuri aedificii, wisdom for the present purpose, skill in contriving and building, a notion of the future edifice.
paragraphs.anchor: And the Lord gave Solomon wisdom

paragraphs.text: A brotherly covenant, which though Tyre some while forgot, {Amo 1:9} and insulted over Jerusalem, yet it was foretold - and accordingly fulfilled - that Tyre, when converted, should leave hoarding and heaping her wealth, and should find another manner of employment for it, viz., to feed and clothe God’s saints. {Isa 23:18}
paragraphs.anchor: And they two made a league together.

paragraphs.text: Heb., A tribute of men, perhaps of aliens, or such as the Gibeonites were in Israel.
paragraphs.anchor: And king Solomon raised a levy.

paragraphs.text: Superiors must make the yokes of their inferiors as easy as is possible, lest they lose their affections, and procure their imprecations.
paragraphs.anchor: Ten thousand a month by courses.

paragraphs.text: To order it, and to see the work done.
paragraphs.anchor: And Adoniram was over the levy.

paragraphs.text: Under which expression are also contained wagoners, mariners, horse keepers, mule drivers, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: That bare burdens.

paragraphs.text: Hewers both of stone and of wood. Eupolemus counteth upon many more.
paragraphs.anchor: Hewers in the mountains.

paragraphs.text: And three hundred more to rule over these rulers, {2Ch 2:2} and all little enough to make the work to go forward as it should.
paragraphs.anchor: Which ruled over the people.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Marble of all sorts, as porphyry, parian, ophites, sphengites, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: Great stones, costly stones, and hewed stones

paragraphs.text: Even those stones that were laid in the base of the building were not rugged and rude, but hewn and costly. God is not all for the eye: he pleaseth himself with the hidden value of the living stones of his spiritual temple.
paragraphs.anchor: To lay the foundation of the house.

paragraphs.text: And Hiram’s builders did hew them.] In Lebanon was the temple framed; in Zion set up: neither hammer nor axe was heard in that holy structure. There was nothing but noise in Lebanon; nothing in Zion, but silence and peace. Whatever tumults are abroad, it is fit - saith a right reverend writer {a} here - there should be all quietness and concord in the Church.

Or Giblites, who were heathens, {Eze 27:9} neighbours to the Sidonians, worshippers of Adonis, saith Strabo, yet used about the holy temple. Ye may likewise make use of human learning in ecclesiastical exercises, but not for ostentation; for that is to make a calf of the treasure gotten out of Egypt.
paragraphs.anchor: And the stone squarers.
